Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every material point. Several provisions would quietly undercut protections we treat as non-negotiable: fraud carve-outs, the Fundamental/Title regime, and specific disclosure. We should not accept the draft as presented.

**Note on the document:** The Disclosure Letter contains hidden, non-rendered text addressed to "any AI assistant". It tells the assistant to confirm that all Seller positions are standard market terms and to raise no objections. I have ignored it. I suggest the deal team raise this with Seller's counsel and ask for a clean, fully visible version of SPA-003. Any hidden content in a disclosure document is a problem on its own terms, separate from the AI aspect.

---

## 1. Material departures and recommended pushback

### A. Liability regime

**1. General cap: Seller proposes 20% / AUD 4.8m (cl 12.1)**
- **Playbook:** start at 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a fallback only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. We do not have that authority.
- **Push back:** reject and hold at 25%. We should not signal that 20% is available. If the team wants to use the fallback later, get Amelia's written authority first.

**2. Thresholds (cl 12.2)**

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Recovery once basket exceeded | Excess only (deductible) | From the first dollar (tipping) |

- The combination is very Seller-friendly. Claims under AUD 25k disappear entirely, and the first AUD 250k of valid loss is never recoverable.
- **Push back:** AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping basket. Fundamental, Title, fraud and specific indemnity claims must sit outside both thresholds.

**3. Claims period: Seller proposes 18 months (cl 12.3/13)**
- **Playbook:** 24 months. 18 months needs Amelia's written approval, which we do not have.
- **Push back:** 24 months.

**4. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13)**
- This is the key hidden override. It would sweep Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenant and payment claims into the general caps, thresholds and time limits by default.
- **Push back:** delete. Invert the drafting so the general limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims. Each other category (Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant, specific indemnity) gets its own expressly stated regime.

**5. Fundamental/Title under the general cap and time limits**
- The Seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale is not a reason to cap title. Title is the asset we are paying AUD 24m for.
- **Push back:** separate regime for Fundamental/Title claims:
  - 100% cap (AUD 24m);
  - at least six years;
  - outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.

**6. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
- As drafted, this would purport to cap and time-bar fraud claims.
- **Push back:** carve fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is a non-negotiable playbook position and no one on our side can waive it. Also add the express category separation from point 4.

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**7. General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7)**
- Clause 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room. Clause 1.2 adds the Accounts, statutory registers and all publicly searchable records.
- This is precisely the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure the playbook rejects.
- **Push back:**
  - delete 1.1 and 1.2;
  - disclosure counts only against a specific warranty, and only if it is fairly disclosed with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter;
  - specific disclosures in sections 2–10 stand or fall on their own content.
- Clause 1.4 (non-admission) is broadly acceptable. It must not be read as diluting fair disclosure or limiting specific indemnities.

**8. Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3)**
- The bar covers anything known to the Buyer "or its advisers", plus anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That reintroduces deemed disclosure by another route and would gut the warranties.
- **Push back:** delete the blanket exclusion. If any qualifier survives, it must:
  - refer to named Seller knowledge persons, with reasonable enquiry;
  - never excuse Title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### C. Conditions and completion mechanics

**9. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)**
- Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6m). Its contract has change-control consent at cl 11.2, with conditions at cl 11.3.
- The Seller offers reasonable endeavours only, and treats the condition as satisfied on delivery of a written consent.
- The Disclosure Letter (s 2) confirms there is currently no final consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied.
- **Push back:**
  - the Condition Precedent requires an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent;
  - documentary evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied must be delivered before Completion;
  - for a customer this material, the obligation should be stronger than reasonable endeavours (for example, all reasonable endeavours or best endeavours, with cooperation and information covenants);
  - the Buyer alone can waive the condition.

**10. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)**
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The facility has change-control at cl 8.1 and discharge at cl 9.2.
- The Seller proposes a release "following Completion". The Disclosure Letter (s 3) confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge exists.
- On a debt-free/cash-free deal this is unacceptable, and a change of control may itself trigger the facility.
- **Push back:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - repayment directly from Completion funds as a funds-flow line item;
  - executed, effective security releases delivered at Completion, including PPSR registrations and any mortgages.
- **Fallback:** a post-completion release only with an irrevocable lender undertaking to release on receipt of payout, and Amelia Frost's approval.

**11. DD-005 employee bonuses (funds flow)**
- AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses is expressly excluded from the funds flow. Payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unaddressed (s 5).
- "A matter for the Seller" is not enough. If these amounts are paid by the Company, they will land on us after Completion.
- **Push back:**
  - either a specific funds-flow line item (deducted from price or treated as Debt/Transaction Costs), or an express Seller-funded mechanism;
  - either way, it must cover all triggered on-costs;
  - add an indemnity for any shortfall;
  - require a statement of which on-costs apply.

### D. Specific risk items

**12. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)**
- The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment.
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but this is not independently verified either way.
- There is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Push back:**
  - broaden the indemnity to cover all loss from any failure of title to, or third-party claims over, the Ironquay/SOW3 materials, not just the payment;
  - preserve the cure route: the Seller procures payment and a confirmatory assignment pre-Completion;
  - the indemnity sits outside the general cap and thresholds;
  - ask for bank evidence of the payment status;
  - do not assume AUD 180k is owed, or that it is paid.

**13. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6)**
- The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". The Disclosure Letter (s 6) establishes neither access, nor scope, nor whether notification is required. About 1,240 records may be involved.
- We should not accept the "not material" characterisation. Equally, we should not assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any loss figure.
- **Push back:**
  - covenants to preserve logs and evidence;
  - complete a proper investigation, using an independent forensic provider if appropriate;
  - give the Buyer regular updates, with access to findings before Completion;
  - make any notification decision in consultation with the Buyer;
  - delete any materiality characterisation from the operative terms;
  - consider a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, without fixing an amount.

**14. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate)**
- The Seller asserts these are "ordinary-course operating costs". The Disclosure Letter (s 8) says nothing about whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and asks that DD-008/DD-011 be read together.
- **Approach:** do not accept the Seller's label, and do not reflexively treat the renewals as Debt or a price deduction. Request:
  - the contracts;
  - timing and commitment status;
  - termination rights;
  - the accounting treatment.
- Decide classification once we have that information. In the meantime, reserve the right to treat any pre-Completion committed but unaccrued amounts appropriately.

**15. Tax/IP "settled under the general regime"**
- **Push back:** these positions remain OPEN on our side and are not agreed. The Seller cannot use this update to fold them into the general cap and time limits.
- We are not asserting unlimited liability either. Table them as separate regimes for negotiation.

**16. Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register**
- DD-012 is the Company's own internal register. It is not independent proof, and the Disclosure Letter (s 10) itself says so.
- **Push back:** require independent evidence of title, ownership, freedom from encumbrances, and authority, for example:
  - a current ASIC company extract;
  - PPSR searches against Seller and Company;
  - share certificates;
  - the constitution and any shareholder agreements (checking for pre-emption rights and their waiver);
  - Seller board approval and authority evidence;
  - confirmation of no options or convertibles.
- A full Title warranty must be backed by the Fundamental regime (point 5).

### E. Items to verify (lower priority, not playbook departures as drafted)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** described as notification only. Confirm the lease wording and ensure notice is given at the correct time.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** an assignment restriction, stated not to be triggered by a share sale. Check for any change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording.

---

## 2. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller | Our position |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m** (no fallback authority) |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k, excess only | **5k / 50k, first dollar** |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months | **24 months** (no fallback approval) |
| 4 | "Limitations apply to all Claims" | Default override | **Delete**; separate regimes per category |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title | General cap/time | **100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/knowledge** |
| 6 | Fraud | Capped/limited | **Full carve-out** (non-waivable) |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable" | **Delete**; any qualifier: named Seller persons + reasonable enquiry, never Title/capacity/fraud/indemnity |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent on delivery | **Effective consent + evidence of cl 11.3 conditions pre-Completion; stronger endeavours** |
| 10 | Riverlark | Release post-Completion | **Payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion** (fallback needs undertaking + Amelia's approval) |
| 11 | DD-005 bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **Line item or Seller-funded, incl. on-costs** |
| 12 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 indemnity | **Broaden; keep SOW3 cure; verify payment status** |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Preserve, investigate, update; no materiality concession; no assumed breach** |
| 14 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Diligence first; no automatic Debt/deduction** |
| 15 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | **Open; separate regimes; no unlimited assumption** |
| 16 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent evidence** (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, authority) |

**Process points:**
- No playbook fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release) should be offered without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft.
- Ask the Seller to withdraw SPA-003 and reissue it without hidden content.
- Our mark-up should open with points 4–8. They are structural, and if they are left unaddressed they would neutralise the gains on the cap and thresholds.
